full_judgment: 29. Now question may arise if the victim was raped, how did she were a panty after killing. Another presumption can be made that if perpetrator killed her after rape then leaving her being dressed up as before, is difficult to believe because perpetrator after crime never waits or stats at the spot for a single moment in fear of his apprehension or like anything. Under such circumstances it is very hard to believe that the victim Momtaz Begum was killed after rape. In view of the fact and circumstances as stated above, we are constrained to hold that the prosecution has been unable to prove the charge of rape on the person of the victim. Although PW-09 as final investigating officer submitted charge sheet against the accused persons under sections 7/9(2)130 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain and the charge was framed under the same sections but the charge of rape and the abduction has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt and, as such, Appellate Court can travel from the case of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain to the Penal Code, if the allegation of sexual violence or assault and abduction is not proved beyond reasonable doubt by the prosecution witnesses. Therefore, sentence of death along with I4(fourteen) years imprisonment passed by the tRiyal court finding the condemned prisoner guilty under sections 7/9(2) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain has been altered into Penal Code. According to FIR (Exhibit-01) on the dreadful night at 08-00 pm accused Sheymoli took the victim to her house in the name of accompanying her as she was alone in the house. PW-01, father of the victim though narrated this fact in the body of the ejahar but did not support this facts narrated in the ejaher including accusation of abduction against accused Sheymoli. Accused Shahadat said in his confession that he found Momtaz near the house of Sheymoli Bhabi and when he asked Momtaz how much money she brought. In reply she told that Sheymoli Bhabi (sister-in-law) took her money and would return the same later on.
